slides.texte_overlay:
habits that will make you
unreasonably confident

checking every bill

read every bill and receipt this month, line by line, and question anything that's wrong. people who check quietly get respected, and people who never look get overcharged.

naming a number first

the next time someone asks what you want to be paid or what you'd charge, say a number first and stop talking. the silence after a number is where confident people win.

the 24 hour rule

wait 24 hours before buying anything that isn't food. not needing to buy things to feel better is a kind of confidence most ads are designed to take away from you.

money history

spend 5 minutes a day on how money actually works: the history of coins, how banks were born, why prices rise. people who understand money stop being so scared of it.

is there any way

once a week, ask "is there any way to..." before accepting a no: an upgrade, a later deadline, a better table. most rules quietly bend for people who ask politely and clearly.
